what: Approve can assign the ticket yet leave the escalation PENDING
note: assignTicket commits, then a separate crossZoneEscalation.update sets APPROVED. No shared transaction. A crash between them strands the escalation PENDING on an already-assigned ticket; the retry then hits :163 ALREADY_ASSIGNED and returns without reconciling, so the row is stuck in the CSM queue forever. override.assignTicket already exposes an `inTransaction` callback (#325 RC-9) built for exactly this and approve does not pass it. BACKLOG HYPOTHESIS CONFIRMED LIVE.

what: Sweep notify failure hides a Platinum escalation from the CSM forever
note: create + audit + notify are three non-transactional writes inside the per-ticket loop with no try/catch (:99-115); a throw in notifyCrossZoneQueue aborts the whole sweep for every later ticket too. The idempotency predicate is `crossZoneEscalations: { none: {} }` (:83) — ANY escalation row ever, in any status — so the half-written ticket is permanently excluded from future sweeps. Same predicate also means a Platinum ticket whose escalation was DENIED can never auto-escalate again. Contrast flag() :127-130 which correctly filters on status in PENDING/DEFERRED. BACKLOG HYPOTHESIS CONFIRMED LIVE.

what: CSM backup actions are audited as the CSM's own, acting tag dropped
note: Every rung of the acting-as cascade exists — banner at AppShell.tsx:69, X-Acting-As-Zone at authHeaders.ts:13, resolution at request-actor.ts:27 — but cross-zone.controller.ts:113 hardcodes actedAsRole:null on all five write endpoints, so every audit row for a backup action is stamped as the CSM acting as themselves. zmOwnsZone :287 reads actedAsRole and is therefore a dead branch. Other modules do it right (batches.controller.ts:129).

what: No UI anywhere for a ZM to flag a Gold/Silver ticket cross-zone
note: Backend flag() and apiCrossZoneFlag both exist; grep over apps/admin/src returns zero call sites for apiCrossZoneFlag. Without it only Platinum auto-escalations ever reach the CSM queue and the entire Gold/Silver manual-escalation half of the tier model is unreachable from the app. s1 scopeNote calls the flag origin boundary-adjacent (ZM ticket list), so the control belongs on the ticket surface, not CrossZonePage.

what: Denied Platinum cannot be re-escalated: row vanishes and no button
note: reEscalateToOps (:201) is the only escape hatch for a denied Platinum, but listForScope :225 lists only PENDING/DEFERRED/ESCALATED_TO_OPS so a DENIED row is invisible in the queue, apiCrossZoneReEscalate has zero call sites, and the actions column is gated to deciders (:122) while the endpoint is ZONAL_MANAGER-only (controller :103) — the one role authorised to press it is the one role the page shows no buttons to. State ESCALATED_TO_OPS is therefore unreachable through the UI.

what: Approve asks for zone id and SE id via browser prompt boxes
note: approve/deny/defer all use window.prompt (:56,:58,:64,:70,:72). The CSM must know a numeric zone id and an SE user id by heart, with no candidate list, no capacity view and no distance signal — the one decision the module exists to make is made blind. Compounding it, nothing validates that seId actually belongs to targetZoneId: the service stores both independently (:170-171) and override.assignTicket only checks the TICKET's home zone (override.service.ts:666), so targetZoneId is an unvalidated label on the record.

what: Deferred escalations never resurface on their review date
note: defer() persists reviewDate (:271) and nothing ever reads it as a trigger — grep for reviewDate outside this module returns no sweep, no cron, no ordering. DEFERRED rows do stay listed (:225) so nothing is lost, but the review date is decoration: a defer-to-Friday and a defer-to-December look identical in the queue, and the CSM has no due-today lens. Softer than the backlog framing but real.

what: No report of who approved what: only the live queue is readable
note: listForScope filters to PENDING/DEFERRED/ESCALATED_TO_OPS, so APPROVED and DENIED rows are write-only once decided; grep over apps/backend/src/reports and /dashboard for crossZoneEscalation or CROSS_ZONE_APPROVE returns nothing. The Ops Head has no way to see which zones lean on CSM backup. The decidedByUserId/decidedByRole/decidedAt columns are already populated (:174-176), so this is a read surface over existing data, not new capture.

what: Decision notice silently skipped when the home zone has no manager
note: notifyHomeZm returns early with no log and no fallback when zone.zonalManagerUserId is null (:320) — precisely the absent-ZM case that makes the CSM backup cascade exist in the first place. The deny/defer reverse path is a notification only (the ticket never moves, by design :62), so dropping the notification drops the whole reverse path for that zone. Fallback should be the CSM/OH pool that already resolves at :298.

what: Static scanner misses audit written one hop deeper in a helper
note: DEV-PROCESS, not a feature gap; excluded from the ranked backlog. static.md:14 claims 6 write-verb endpoints have no audit write — 6 of 6 FALSE. Every write path audits through the single private helper auditEscalation, which calls prisma.auditLog.create at :367 (action, entityType cross_zone_escalation, actorRole, actedAsRole): sweep :110, flag :144, approve :179, re-escalate :211, deny and defer via decide :277. Module-wide grep for withAudit(|audit.record(|auditLog.create returns exactly one site, :367, reached by all five. NO P2 FILED. Matches the scheduling (11/11 false) and tickets (8/10 false) measurements: the column under-detects one delegation hop, never invents. The real audit defect is CZ-03 (actedAsRole always null), not a missing row.

what: Approve assigns the ticket then 500s, stranding the escalation PENDING
note: WALKED 2026-09-02, E4, and it is NOT a race - it is deterministic. POST /cross-zone/<id>/approve as csm@fsm.test with seId fffebec6-17e6-4467-9f3c-d1e1b1fa317c returned HTTP 500 six times in a row (correlationIds 4e41c498, 55befbed, 31a990ba, 617f38ee, 3cd8f65e, 6ac814c3). Phase 1 COMMITTED every time: tickets de005f2f / e634693a / db248a3f / b7049f9f / ffa60017 / a57902d6 are now FORMALLY_ASSIGNED to Amit Sharma on schedule 1185. Phase 2 never ran: escalations 4-9 all read status PENDING, targetZoneId null, in GET /cross-zone as CSM. Retry returns 409 TICKET_ALREADY_ASSIGNED (:163) forever with no reconciliation, and the queue row exposes no assignment state, so the CSM sees six rows demanding a decision that is already made. The only escape is deny, which writes DENIED onto an escalation whose ticket is assigned (walked on esc 3, HTTP 200) - a false record. override.assignTicket exposes an inTransaction hook (#325 RC-9, override.service.ts:659) built for exactly this and approve does not pass it. WHAT THREW is not isolated (no backend log file on disk); the CONSEQUENCE is E4.

what: Target zone is never told: no notice, no queue row, no schedule
note: HAND-OFF TEST, walked end to end 2026-09-02. 1 UPSTREAM pass: ZM flag -> esc 1, CSM and OH both got CROSS_ZONE_MANUAL_FLAG carrying escalationId and ticketId. 2 CARRIER pass: CSM approve (targetZoneId 2, seId 0bbe6100 Ramesh Rao, zone 2) -> ticket 30732620 FORMALLY_ASSIGNED, schedule 1238, batch 1758, nothing retyped. 3 DOWNSTREAM FAIL: as zm.south@fsm.test (the receiving zone) GET /notifications = 0 items, GET /cross-zone = 0 rows (listForScope :225 clamps on homeZoneId), GET /tickets/30732620 = 404 TICKET_NOT_FOUND, and GET /schedules omits 1238 entirely. The ONLY zone-2-visible trace is Ramesh Rao activeTicketCount moving 3 -> 4 on GET /engineers: a number with no name. 4 PAYLOAD FAIL. 5 REVERSE FAIL: deny on the APPROVED escalation returns 409 ESCALATION_NOT_ACTIONABLE - once approved a cross-zone hand-off cannot be withdrawn through this module. 6 IDENTITY FAIL: GET /batches/1758 carries no escalationId and no cross-zone marker. RESULT MANUAL. Aggravating and separately fixable: schedule 1238 is stamped zoneId 1 / North (the ticket home zone) although its SE lives in zone 2, so the target ZM schedules list hides their own engineer day while the home ZM sees a schedule for an engineer who is not theirs.

what: Home ZM decision notice reaches nobody: routed by a stale pointer
note: UPGRADED E2 -> E4 and the cause is wider than the null check. Two independent decisions on zone-1 escalations - approve (esc 1) and deny (esc 3) - produced ZERO notifications for zm.north@fsm.test (User.zoneId 1, role ZONAL_MANAGER): GET /notifications returned 0 items both before and after. notifyHomeZm :318 resolves ONE denormalised pointer, zones.zonal_manager_user_id, which seed-mock-engineers.ts:109 aims at a different user (zm-z1@mock.fsm), so the human actually managing zone 1 is never a recipient. Contrast notifyCrossZoneQueue :289, which resolves recipients BY ROLE via usersInRoles and did deliver to both csm@fsm.test and ops.head@fsm.test in the same walk. Fix is to route the decision notice by role+zone like the queue notice already does, with the CSM/OH pool as the fallback the original :320 early-return has none of.

what: ZM flag endpoint is alive and correct; no UI anywhere calls it
note: NO PATH ruled out - this is C4 (no UI), the cheaper half. POST /cross-zone/flag as zm.north returned 200 result OK escalationId 1 and the row was readable back in GET /cross-zone as CSM, ZM and OH. Perms are correct as built: zm.south flagging a zone-1 ticket -> 403 TICKET_OUT_OF_ZONE, ops.head -> 403, se.north -> 403, csm -> 200 in any zone (intended: @Roles :56 names CSM). Persist and downstream both pass: CSM and OH each received CROSS_ZONE_MANUAL_FLAG with escalationId and ticketId in metadata. The whole capability works and no screen can reach it - grep over apps/admin/src still returns zero call sites for apiCrossZoneFlag, so the Gold/Silver manual-escalation half of the tier model is unreachable from the app. Cost is a button on the ZM ticket surface, not a backend build.

what: Re-escalate is ZM-only at the API and ZM-invisible in the UI
note: ROLE GATE WALKED. POST /cross-zone/3/re-escalate: zm.north 409 NOT_A_DENIED_AUTO_ESCALATION (guard passed, reached the service), zm.south 409 (same - the type check at :204 runs before zmOwnsZone :205, so a foreign ZM learns the escalation exists), csm 403, ops.head 403, se 403. So the endpoint is alive and genuinely ZONAL_MANAGER-only, while CrossZonePage.tsx:122 renders the actions column only for deciders (CSM/OH): the one authorised role is the one role the page shows no buttons to. Compounded by listForScope :225, which lists only PENDING/DEFERRED/ESCALATED_TO_OPS - a DENIED row is invisible in the queue even to the ZM who would press the button. apiCrossZoneReEscalate still has zero call sites. State ESCALATED_TO_OPS remains unreachable through the UI.

what: Flag accepts a ticket that is already formally assigned
note: WALKED. Ticket 30732620 was FORMALLY_ASSIGNED (via the approve of esc 1) and flag() still accepted it: POST /cross-zone/flag as zm.north -> 200, escalationId 3. flag() checks tier, zone and prior ACTIVE escalation (:127-130) but never assignmentState, so an escalation can be raised for work that is already covered. That escalation is then permanently unapprovable - approve hits the ALREADY_ASSIGNED short-circuit at :163 - which is the cheapest route into the CZ-01 orphan state and does not need a crash to get there. Blocks CZ-01 claim that the orphan is only reachable by a race.

what: Approve 404 lies: every non-OK assign outcome reads as not-found
note: WALKED. approve :167 collapses every assignTicket result that is not OK or ALREADY_ASSIGNED into result NOT_FOUND, which controller :118 renders as HTTP 404 ESCALATION_OR_SE_NOT_FOUND. AssignOutcome also carries CONFLICT_DEFERRED and REASON_REQUIRED (override.service.ts:148-150). Reproduced on escalation 2 / ticket 5dbbd40c: the escalation exists (readable in GET /cross-zone), the SE exists (0bbe6100 assigned successfully elsewhere in the same walk) and the ticket exists and is UNASSIGNED - yet approve returns 404 twice, with two different SEs. The CSM is told the record is missing when the real answer is most likely a return-date deferral they are allowed to override with a reason. The deferral escape hatch (#249 confirm + reasonCode) is not plumbed through approve at all, so the row is unactionable and undiagnosable from the app.

what: Sweep one-shot predicate untestable: zero Platinum tickets exist
note: UNTESTABLE, and say so plainly. 6500 tickets scanned via GET /tickets as CSM (paged limit=500): 6500 SILVER, 0 PLATINUM, 0 GOLD. POST /cross-zone/sweep as CSM returns 200 escalated 0 - which proves nothing, because nothing qualifies. Capability C1, crit 5, the reason this module exists, has never fired in this environment. FIXTURE THAT WOULD SETTLE IT: one PLATINUM ticket, status OPEN, assignmentState UNASSIGNED, no deferredUntil, lastStateChangedAt older than 240 min (or 60 min with a CRITICAL+ slaBucket), in a zone with a real ZM. Half of the hypothesis IS now E4 by the adjacent path: flag() re-escalated ticket 30732620 a second time after its first escalation reached APPROVED (esc 3, HTTP 200), so the status-scoped predicate at :127-130 and the sweep none-ever predicate at :83 demonstrably disagree about whether one escalation per ticket is the rule. Which is intended still cannot be read off the code. Perms half settled: sweep is 403 for ZM, WM and SE.

what: Acting-as tag dropped: no perms hole, but the audit trail is wrong
note: H-CZ-4 P4 FRAMING IS FALSIFIED - the strongestAlternative wins, and CZ-03 is re-coded P4 -> P2. Role walk over all five write endpoints: flag ZM 200 in own zone / 403 TICKET_OUT_OF_ZONE out of zone, CSM 200 any zone (intended, @Roles :56 names CSM), OH 403, SE 403; sweep CSM and OH 200, ZM/WM/SE 403; deny ZM/WM/SE 403; re-escalate ZM only, CSM/OH/SE 403; GET WM and SE 403. Every gate behaves exactly as the decorators say. The dead actedAsRole branch at zmOwnsZone :288 changes NO permission outcome, in either direction - CSM breadth on flag is granted by the decorator, not by the dead branch. So this is not a separation-of-duties breach. What remains is real and unchanged in price: controller :113 hardcodes actedAsRole null, so every backup action a CSM takes in an absent ZM zone is stamped in audit_log as the CSM acting as themselves, and the acting-as cascade (AppShell.tsx:69 banner, authHeaders.ts:13 header, request-actor.ts:27 resolution) is decorative on this surface. Other modules pass it through (batches.controller.ts:129).

what: Target zone id is free text and unvalidated; mismatch not persisted
note: PARTIALLY SETTLED, honest about the rest. Confirmed by code and schema read plus a walk: schema.prisma:600 gives targetZoneId no relation and no FK, and the service stores it (:170) beside assignedSeId (:171) with no comparison; override.assignTicket only ever checks the TICKET home zone (override.service.ts:666) and looks the engineer up by id alone (:668). CrossZonePage.tsx:56-60 collects both values from window.prompt with no picker. NOT SETTLED: no mismatched pair was actually persisted. Six attempts to approve with targetZoneId 999 all died in the CZ-01 phase-2 500 before the escalation row was written, and the one approve that completed (esc 1) used a consistent pair. FIXTURE THAT WOULD SETTLE IT: fix CZ-01 first, then approve any PENDING escalation with targetZoneId 999 and a real seId and re-GET /cross-zone to see whether targetZoneId 999 persists. Until then the per-zone metric claim is E2, not E4. Note the walk found a DIFFERENT and confirmed zone-labelling defect in the same family - see CZ-11: the schedule minted by a cross-zone approve is stamped with the HOME zone, not the SE zone.
